title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the neighbouring pages). S is a regular connected scheme of finite type over Q. k is the algebraic closure of Q in Γ(S,O_S), so S/k is geometrically connected, and K is presumably the base or function field over which P lives. M is a finitely generated Tannakian category of smooth semisimple motives over S. With a Betti fibre functor T at ξ∈S(C), G = Aut⊗(T) and M ≅ Rep(G). P = Isom⊗(T_B,T_DR) is a G-torsor carrying an integrable (Gauss–Manin) connection and a ⊗-filtration (Hodge filtration). Its Hodge data are encoded by cocharacters i1, i2 and the parabolic H' ⊂ G'. On the previous page there is a holomorphic, monodromy-equivariant period map f from the universal cover of S(C) to the space Y_G of homomorphisms from Deligne's torus Res_{C/R}G_m to G_R.

This page states two things.

(10) Modulo the Hodge conjecture, the identity component G^0 is the smallest Q-algebraic subgroup containing the image of the Hodge cocharacter i1^C. In modern terms: the connected motivic Galois group equals the Mumford–Tate group. The marginal NB says the genericity condition, i.e. taking a Hodge-generic point, is vacuous when K is algebraic.

The page then sets R = the Zariski closure in G of the monodromy image w(π1(S(C),ξ)). Using (9), the homotopy exact sequence 1→π1(S_kbar)→π1(S)→Gal(kbar/k)→1 together with density of π1^top in π1(S_kbar), R is normal in G. By (4), the ℓ-adic/adelic Galois representation π1(S)→G(A)→G̃(A), with G̃ = G/R, kills the geometric fundamental group. It therefore factors through ũ: Gal(kbar/k)→G̃(A).

(11) Modulo Hodge, the quotient torsor P̃ = P/R under G̃, with its induced connection, has trivial monodromy. Hence it 'descends to k': there is a G̃_k-torsor P̃_0 over k with P̃ ≅ P̃_0⊗_k K. For every G̃-module M, the descent datum on P×^G M (the bundle of flat sections) is compatible with the Hodge filtration, i.e. the filtration is horizontal. Consequently the following all descend to k:
- the image H̃' = Im(H'→G̃') of the filtration-stabiliser;
- the torsor Q̃ = Q×^{H'}H̃' of filtered trivialisations;
- the induced cocharacters i1, i2 : G_m→G̃'', descending to (ĩ1)_0, (ĩ2)_0 : G_{m,k}→G̃''_0.

In modern language: the quotient of the generic motivic Galois group by the (Zariski closure of the) geometric monodromy is the motivic Galois group of a constant motive over k, with its full de Rham, Hodge and Galois structure. Equivalently, the 'fixed part' of a smooth family of motives is a motive over k (a motivic theorem of the fixed part / motivic homotopy exact sequence). This serves the general programme of describing the motivic Galois group of a family: generic Mumford–Tate group = monodromy ⋊/extension by a constant motivic group.
errors: 'G^0 engendré par i1^C' must be read at a Hodge-generic point. At special points the Mumford–Tate group can be smaller than the generic one; the marginal NB on 'généricité' shows Grothendieck was aware of this. He also means the smallest Q-subgroup whose C-points contain the image of i1^C, which automatically contains the conjugate cocharacter and the weight.

The descent of P/R to k uses more than Hodge. Trivial monodromy gives only analytic triviality over S(C). Algebraicity of the flat sections needs regularity of Gauss–Manin (Deligne 1970). Descent from C (or K) to k needs Galois equivariance plus S geometrically connected over k. These steps are not spelled out.

Horizontality of the Hodge filtration on the flat-section bundle is precisely the theorem of the fixed part (Griffiths/Deligne, proved ~1970–71). Here it is presented as a consequence of the descent datum (modulo Hodge), so it is a conditional step.
The struck-out block on G̃', R', H̃' is left inconsistent and is reworked in the final bracket. Notation G', G'', H', H'' is not defined on this page.

ideas.what: Modulo the Hodge conjecture, the connected motivic Galois group of a motive equals the smallest Q-group containing the Hodge cocharacter (the Mumford–Tate group)
ideas.modern_name: Motivic Galois group = Mumford–Tate group under the Hodge conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore from Grothendieck/Serre; Mumford 1966 (Hodge group); made explicit in Saavedra 1972 and Deligne–Milne 1982
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA. Grothendieck's motivic Galois group ideas reached print via Saavedra's thesis and Serre's later accounts.

ideas.what: Zariski closure of geometric monodromy is a normal subgroup of the motivic Galois group of the generic fibre, via the étale homotopy exact sequence
ideas.modern_name: Normality of connected monodromy in the (generic) Mumford–Tate / motivic group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II, 1971, semisimplicity/fixed part); Y. André 1992 (Compositio, monodromy normal in derived MT group); André 1996 for motivated motives

ideas.what: The quotient torsor P/R with trivial monodromy, together with its Hodge filtration and Hodge cocharacters, descends to the field of constants k
ideas.modern_name: Theorem of the fixed part (motivic version): global flat sections form a constant motive over k
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths, Deligne (Hodge II 4.1.2) for Hodge structures; André 1996 ('Pour une théorie inconditionnelle des motifs') for motivated motives

ideas.what: Galois representation of π1(S) into G(A) factoring through Gal(kbar/k) modulo monodromy
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of ℓ-adic realisation with the motivic homotopy exact sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Deligne; later Esnault–Hai type Tannakian exact sequences)

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck formulated, conditionally on the Hodge conjecture, a motivic theorem of the fixed part. The quotient of the motivic group of a family by the Zariski closure of monodromy is the motivic group of a constant motive over k, and the Hodge filtration and Hodge cocharacters descend. This predates Deligne's fixed-part theorem (1971) and André's normality/fixed-part results (1992/1996), which are not credited to Grothendieck.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and attribution. It shows that the relative motivic Galois group / monodromy picture, now central in work on Mumford–Tate domains and André–Oort-type questions, was already in Grothendieck's framework in 1965.

missed.claim: Explicit 1965 statement that, modulo the Hodge conjecture, G^0 is generated by the Hodge cocharacter. This is the Mumford–Tate group being identified with the motivic Galois group, contemporaneous with or slightly before Mumford's 1966 Hodge-group paper.
missed.quote: (Modulo conjecture de Hodge) G^0 est engendré sur Q par i1^C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's direct role in the Hodge-theoretic description of motivic Galois groups, usually attributed diffusely to Serre/Deligne/Mumford.

deep.surprise_reason: No new mathematics by today's standards: the statements are now theorems or folklore (Deligne, André). Historically notable, though: in 1965, conditionally on Hodge, Grothendieck has motivic group = Mumford–Tate, normality of monodromy, and descent of the fixed part with its Hodge data to the constant field. These are years before the published versions and are uncredited to him.
transcription_corrections: '(P̃, C̃) avec sa connexion intégrable' should read '(P̃, G̃)', i.e. the torsor P̃ under G̃, with its connection.
'G̃'_0 = Aut_{G̃_k}(P̃_0)': in the image the subscript is G̃_k and the whole block is struck out.

Final bracket reads roughly: '...se descendent respectivement en H̃'_0 ⊂ G̃'_0 et Q̃_0 sous H̃'_0, et (d'où H̃''_0 et G̃''_0 quotients descendant H̃'' et G̃''), et aussi les composés ĩ1, ĩ2 : G_{m,K} → G'' → G̃'' se descendent en (ĩ1)_0, (ĩ2)_0 : G_{m,k} → G̃''_0'.
Marginal note: 'NB la généricité est vide si K est alg.' (reading plausible).
